options.text: Yes because repeated h2 levels are allowed.
No because h2 cannot repeat.
Yes because only the first level matters.
No because h4 skips the expected h3 level.

questions.explanation: The jump from h2 to h4 skips h3, breaking the outline. Repeated h2 is fine, but the skip is not.

questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.stem: A clerk wants an h2 to look smaller than an h3; is that allowed?

options.text: Yes because size is presentation and level is structure.
No because heading levels fix font sizes.
No because CSS cannot override heading sizes.
Yes but only if the h3 is disabled.

questions.explanation: Presentation can override default sizes without changing structural level. Level fixes meaning, not pixels.

questions.topic: What a form actually submits
questions.stem: A clerk submits a form with method get; where does the data appear?

options.text: In the request body only, never the URL.
Nowhere because get does not submit data.
In the query string of the URL.
In a cookie automatically.

questions.explanation: GET appends form data to the URL query string. Body-only or no-submission assumptions misread the method.

questions.stem: A clerk needs to preserve multiple spaces in a code listing; which CSS helps?

options.text: white-space normal, which collapses spaces.
font-size zero, which removes spaces.
color transparent, which hides spaces.
white-space pre, which preserves spaces.

questions.topic: The outer width under the initial box-sizing
questions.learningObjective: Compute outer width with asymmetric padding
questions.stem: A clerk sets width 150px, padding-left 10px, padding-right 30px, border 5px each side; outer width?

options.text: 200px because padding and border add to width.
190px because only left padding is added.
150px because width includes padding and border.
170px because border is ignored.

questions.explanation: Content-box adds both paddings and both borders: 150+10+30+5+5=200px. Partial addition understates it.

questions.topic: The content width under border-box sizing
questions.learningObjective: Compute content width with asymmetric padding
questions.stem: A clerk uses border-box width 150px with padding-left 10px, padding-right 30px, border 5px each side; content width?

answer.exemplar: The content width is 100px because border-box includes all extras in width, so 150 minus 40 padding minus 10 border leaves 100 pixels for content.

questions.explanation: Border-box subtracts all padding and border from declared width. Ignoring any extra understates the subtraction.

questions.topic: Collapsing two adjoining vertical margins
questions.stem: A clerk separates two blocks with a 1px border between them; do their margins collapse?

options.text: Yes because adjoining margins always collapse.
No because margins are removed by borders.
Yes because borders do not affect margins.
No because the border prevents collapse.

questions.explanation: A border between blocks separates the margins, preventing collapse. Universal collapse assumptions miss separators.

questions.topic: A percentage padding against the containing block
questions.stem: A clerk nests an element with padding 10% inside a 500px container; padding in px?

50px because percentage padding resolves against element width.
0px because nested elements cannot use percent padding.
500px because full container width is used.

questions.explanation: Percentage padding resolves against the containing block width, 50px. Element-width or denial assumptions misread the rule.

questions.topic: Chaining a rem length into an em length

16px because rem ignores font sizes.

128px because em and rem multiply.

questions.topic: A viewport unit against the window height
questions.stem: A clerk sets size 10vmin on a 800x600 viewport; how many pixels result?

options.text: 140px because vmin adds both dimensions.
80px because vmin uses the larger dimension.
10px because vmin counts absolute pixels.
60px because vmin uses the smaller dimension.

questions.explanation: vmin is one percent of the smaller viewport dimension, so 10vmin equals 60px. Larger-dimension or pixel readings misread it.

questions.topic: A full width row that overflows because of its padding
questions.stem: A clerk sees horizontal scroll on a 100% width row with padding; which fix applies?

options.text: Remove all padding from the row.
Add overflow hidden to hide the scroll.
Change width to 50% to compensate.
Switch box-sizing to border-box.

questions.explanation: Border-box folds padding into width, eliminating overflow without removing padding. Hiding or guessing widths treats symptoms.
questions.hint: Fix the box model, not the symptom.

questions.topic: Choosing padding to reach a target outer width
questions.stem: A clerk uses border-box width 300px with content 260px and 5px border each side; what padding total fits?

40px total because border is ignored.
50px total because border is doubled.
0px because border-box removes padding.

questions.explanation: Border-box width includes content, padding, and border, so padding totals 300-260-10=30px. Ignoring border overstates padding.

questions.topic: Percentage padding then the outer width it produces
questions.stem: A clerk sets width 100% and padding 5% on content-box; why might the page scroll horizontally?

options.text: Because 100% means 100 pixels.

Because padding converts the element to inline.

questions.explanation: Content-box adds percentage padding beyond the full width, causing overflow. Invalidity or unit misreadings are wrong causes.
